panels.figure_caption: Inflammatory HCA (with less typical imaging features): (a) the 5 cm lesion has slight and homogeneous enhancement after microbubble contrast agent injection and (b) becomes isoechoic relative to the adjacent liver parenchyma. (c) The lesion (black arrow) located in segment II is isointense on T1W images with (d) a drop-out signal on chemical shift images and (e) hypointense on T2 fat-suppressed images. (f) The arterial enhancement is slight (g) with a wash out in the delayed phase. (h) Macroscopic picture: well-limited, nonencapsulated tan-colour lesion without haemorrhagic changes. (i, j) The tumour shows moderate telangiectasia (30%, arrow head) mixed with steatotic hepatocytes (40%, black arrow).

plate_findings.evidence: 1.5 cm hypervascular mass in segment 8 of the liver

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is an arterial phase CT scan showing a 1.5 cm hypervascular mass in the liver, consistent with hepatocellular adenoma. The article identifies the lesion as an inflammatory hepatocellular adenoma. B: Panel B is a follow-up arterial phase CT scan demonstrating interval growth of the hypervascular liver mass, consistent with a progressing hepatocellular adenoma.

A hepatic lesion was identified, which increased in size from 15 mm to 43 mm over 47 months (Fig. 1A, B). Serologic tests for hepatitis B and hepatitis C were negative. Tumor markers were as follows: alpha-fetoprotein, 15.5 ng/mL (normal ≤ 8.1); CA 19-9, 100.71 U/mL (normal ≤ 37.0); and protein induced by vitamin K absence (PIVKA-II), 48 mAU/mL (normal ≤ 40). Liver function was preserved, corresponding to a Child–Pugh score of 6, class A.

plate_findings.evidence: Enhanced on the T1-postcontrast arterial phase image

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel shows T1-weighted MRI of a liver mass consistent with a hepatocellular adenoma as reported in the caption. B: Panel shows T2-weighted MRI of a liver mass consistent with a hepatocellular adenoma as reported in the caption. C: Panel demonstrates arterial phase enhancement characteristic of a hepatocellular adenoma. D: Panel demonstrates persistent enhancement in the portal phase of the liver mass, consistent with the description of a hepatocellular adenoma.

panels.figure_caption: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenoma in a patient with MAS. Hypointense mass located on the junction of segments VIII and IV of the liver on axial T1-wieghted image (A), hyperintense on T2-weighted image (B). We can observe enhancement on the T1-postcontrast arterial phase image (C), persistent during the portal phase (D).
in_text_mentions: We also observed a hepatocellular adenoma in a patient with severe MAS. The liver lesion was detected at age 17 years on a follow-up ultrasound, and initially measured 42 mm ( Figure 8 ). The patient was asymptomatic, and she did not use a contraceptive pill. A resection was realized 18 months later because of its rapid growth to 75 mm and the inherent risk of bleeding. Anapathological examination confirmed hepatocellular adenoma without degeneration and the R201C pathogenic variant was detected in resected tissue.

plate_findings.evidence: heterogeneously hyper-enhancing hepatic masses

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrating multiple hyper-enhancing hepatic masses (consistent with hepatocellular adenoma) and a right subcapsular hematoma, which is a known severe presentation of this condition. Both panels show the same pathological features. B: Coronal contrast-enhanced CT showing multiple hyper-enhancing hepatic masses and a right subcapsular hematoma, consistent with the presentation of hepatocellular adenoma.
panels.attribution_text: Rocha et al. Liver Transplantation for Treatment of Unresectable Spontaneous Ruptured Hepatocellular Adenoma: A Rare Indication.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.27788. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography (CT) of the abdomen on the day of presentation. Axial (A) and coronal (B) contrast-enhanced CT images demonstrated heterogeneously hyper-enhancing hepatic masses. The largest was one in the right lobe, which measured 11 cm and one in the left lobe, which measured 6.7 cm. The CT also showed a right subcapsular haematoma with signs of active hemorrhage (arrows) measuring 22x16x10 cm.
